Q: VS Code - Jupyter notebook doesn't automatically select the default kernel A:

I got it to work whenever you create a new ipynb file in a workspace by writing the following in my .vscode/settings.json:

{
    "python.envFile": "path/to/env",
    "jupyter.disableJupyterAutoStart": false,
    "python.defaultInterpreterPath": "path/to/env/python.exe",
    "python.terminal.activateEnvironment": true,
    "python.terminal.activateEnvInCurrentTerminal": true,
    "python.testing.autoTestDiscoverOnSavePattern": "{**/*.py,**/*.ipynb}"
}

I'm not sure which combination of these setting did it, but it seems to work.

Q: How to disable new 'modal window' in VSCode A:

Disable this setting:

Workbench > Editor: Allow Open in Modal Editor

Controls whether editors can be opened in a modal overlay. When enabled, certain editors such as Settings and Keyboard Shortcuts may open in a centered modal overlay instead of as a regular editor tab.

This "feature" is currently only available in the Insider's Build.

Q: Flag a row after conditions met in R A:

You could cummulative sum the condition value == 99 per group and check if it is >= 1 and if so, turn the boolean to integer using +.

dplyr::mutate(X, new = +(cumsum(value == 99) >= 1), .by = id)
# or
transform(X, new = ave(value, id, FUN = \(x) +(cumsum(x == 99) >= 1)))
# or
library(data.table)
setDT(X)[, new := +(cumsum(value == 99) >= 1), by = id][]
# or as @skbaldur pointed out 
setDT(X)[, new := cummax(value == 99), by = id][]
# or collapse
collapse::ftransform(X, new = +(collapse::fcumsum(value == 99, g = id) >= 1)

Benchmark

bench::mark(
  dplyr_cumsum = dplyr::mutate(X, new = +(cumsum(value == 99) >= 1), .by = id),
  dplyr_cumany = dplyr::mutate(X, new = +(dplyr::cumany(value == 99)), .by = id),
  ave_cummax = transform(X,new = ave(value >= 99, id, FUN = cummax)),
  ave_cumsum = transform(X,new = ave(value, id, FUN = \(x) +(cumsum(x == 99) >= 1))),
  collapse = collapse::ftransform(X, new = +(collapse::fcumsum(value == 99, g = id) >= 1)),
  m = transform(X, new = ave(value == 99, id, FUN = \(x) as.integer(Reduce(`|`, x, accumulate = TRUE)))),
  glory = transform(X, new = 1-(Reduce(max, (value>=99)*id, a=T) < id)),
  iterations = 5000
) |> dplyr::arrange(median)

Q: Python Input Queue Issue A:

This happens because the input is buffered by your operating system or shell. The keystrokes pressed during time.sleep are still considered input, and then input() sees that input is already there. Most of the time, these terminal applications/games, in your case, would use a library that wraps around the terminal, putting it in a raw terminal mode. Curses are the widely used one for Python:

In your case, you could just use curses.flushinp() which would flush the input line before you take in your input. I would look into the official curses documentation and how to make a curses session:

https://docs.python.org/3/howto/curses.html
